traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Blade pale green, elliptic-lanceolate, 25-100 cm". Read as 25 to 100 cm.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Leaves monomorphic, evergreen, numerous in vaselike cluster, 40-170 cm"; "Blade ... 25-100 cm". The flora gives no petiole length; the leaf less its blade, read as 15 to 70 cm.

traits.pinnae.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Pinnae not articulate to rachis, in 8-24 pairs". Read as 16 to 48 pinnae.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "narrowly deltate to lanceolate, pinnatifid; proximal to middle pinnae 12-42 × 2.5-8 cm". The pinnae, read as 12 to 42 cm long.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "proximal to middle pinnae 12-42 × 2.5-8 cm". The pinnae, read as 2.5 to 8 cm wide.

traits.stipe_scales.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Petiole straw-colored, sometimes reddish at base; base thickened, with densely set orange scales." Read as dense.

traits.stipe_scale_extent.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "base thickened, with densely set orange scales". Read as base.

traits.stipe_scale_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "densely set orange scales". Read as a brownish orange.

traits.stipe_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Petiole straw-colored, sometimes reddish at base". Read as a pale straw; the reddish base is not drawn.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Stems forming a stout caudex covered with petiole bases, suberect", read as ascending. Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Woodwardia fimbriata (fern-2026-10-15#2267): rhizome short-creeping. Combined on the owner's rule (2026-10-15): where two sources differ, both are kept and the range spans them.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Leaves monomorphic, evergreen". Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) (fern-2026-10-15#2267): evergreen.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Woodwardia fimbriata (fern-2026-10-15#2267): fronds erect-spreading; with Flora of North America's "numerous in vaselike cluster", read as ascending.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Pinnae not articulate to rachis, in 8-24 pairs ... pinnatifid". A pinnate blade; read as compound.

traits.division_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Pinnae ... in 8-24 pairs". Read as pinnate.

traits.division_order.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Woodwardia fimbriata (fern-2026-10-15#2267): pinnate-pinnatifid (from its figure), division order 2; Flora of North America vol. 2: pinnae "pinnatifid".

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Blade pale green, elliptic-lanceolate". Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) (fern-2026-10-15#2267): broadly oblanceolate. Combined on the owner's rule (2026-10-15): where two sources differ, both are kept and the range spans them.

traits.frond_dimorphism.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Leaves monomorphic".

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "scaly-glandular upon emergence but soon glabrate". Read as glabrescent; Hoshizaki and Moran (fern-2026-10-15#2267) give the lower surface glabrous.

traits.sorus_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Sori short and broad, mostly curved and confined to costular areoles, deeply sunken into blades." Read as oblong; their curve is not drawn.

traits.sorus_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): sori "confined to costular areoles", the row of areoles beside each segment's midrib. Read as costal.

traits.indusium.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Indusia cartilaginous and vaulted". A flap over each sorus; read as flap.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): leaves "numerous in vaselike cluster, 40-170 cm". The plant is about as tall as its ascending leaves reach, read as 40 to 150 cm typically, in place of the species-facts estimate of 1 to 2 m (record L3150308).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Woodwardia fimbriata (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): leaves "40-170 cm". At most the longest leaf, 1.7 m, in place of the species-facts estimate of 2.7 m (record L3150308).

generator.params.note: Deer fern's values (blechnum-spicant), for a large vase-forming fern: a thicker rachis (frond_radius 0.004, from 0.0015, as the flora's petiole base is "thickened" and the leaves to 170 cm), pinnae at 70 degrees to the rachis (from 82). Its hand-set angles, droop and pinna_area are dropped, so the fern rules set them from its posture and the look's default; frond length, stipe share, pinna count and sizes come from the stated measures. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.1 m tall at 8 years in the open, within the 40-170 cm leaves Flora of North America gives, leaning out in a vase. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours by eye after Flora of North America vol. 2: "Blade pale green", a light, slightly yellow green. Its stipes take their stated colour (stipe_colour), its scales theirs (stipe_scale_colour). The pinna card is a frond card (the class rule for division order 2) as wide for its length as the flora's pinnae, 2.5-8 by 12-42 cm (0.2), nearly sessile; its segment count is the card's default, as the flora counts none.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
